context_title: BAAI/bgem3 vs KingsoftLLM/QZhouEmbeddingZh vs nvidia/Nemotron3Embed8BBF16 vs jinaai/jinaembeddingsv5omnismall vs Qwen/Qwen3VLEmbedding8B vs Octen/OctenEmbedding8B vs naverai/MuCo7B vs caraai/ALM2Vec

entries.query: BAAI/bgem3 vs KingsoftLLM/QZhouEmbeddingZh vs nvidia/Nemotron3Embed8BBF16 vs jinaai/jinaembeddingsv5omnismall vs Qwen/Qwen3VLEmbedding8B vs Octen/OctenEmbedding8B vs naverai/MuCo7B vs caraai/ALM2Vec
entries.answer:
These models split into three fairly different groups: strong textonly multilingual retrievers, multimodal retrievers, and more specialized Chinese or experimental models, so the “best” choice depends mostly on whether you need textonly RAG, crosslingual retrieval, or textimage/video retrieval. Based on the available modelcard and benchmark information, Octen/OctenEmbedding8B looks strongest for topend text retrieval, BAAI/bgem3 remains the safest lightweight multilingual baseline, Qwen/Qwen3VLEmbedding8B is the most capable multimodal option in your list, and the others are more niche or less fully documented in the sources I could verify.[1][2][3][4]

 What each model is

BAAI/bgem3 is a 568Mparameter multilingual text embedding model built for more than 100 languages, with support for dense retrieval, sparse retrieval, and multivector retrieval, and it can handle inputs up to 8192 tokens. That makes it unusually versatile for classic search and RAG pipelines where you may want one model that can cover multiple retrieval styles without huge compute cost.[5][2]

KingsoftLLM/QZhouEmbeddingZh does not appear directly in the verified results I found, but the closely related KingsoftLLM/QZhouEmbedding model is described as a 7B generalpurpose contextual text embedding model built on Qwen2.57BInstruct, with up to 8k context and claims of first place on MTEB and CMTEB as of August 27, 2025. From that description, it looks especially aimed at strong Chinese and general text embedding performance rather than multimodal retrieval.[4]

nvidia/Nemotron3Embed8BBF16 is described in the verified search results as an 8B multilingual text embedding model optimized for RAG, semantic search, and crosslingual retrieval, with a claim of 1 on the multilingual RTEB leaderboard as of July 2026. That suggests it is likely one of the strongest candidates here if your workload is multilingual text retrieval rather than imagetext search.[6][7]

jinaai/jinaembeddingsv5omnismall was not directly surfaced in the verified pages I found, but a recent embedding comparison article lists Jina models as strong on multimodal and dimensioncompression scenarios, while a broader 2026 roundup highlights the Jina family as competitive in retrieval use cases. Because I could not verify the exact v5omnismall card in the allotted sources, I would treat it as promising but not fully confirmed here.[8][5]

Qwen/Qwen3VLEmbedding8B is an 8B multimodal embedding model that accepts text, images, screenshots, videos, and mixed multimodal input, supports 30+ languages, has 32k context length, and supports output dimensions from 64 to 4096. That makes it the clearest fit in your list for multimodal retrieval systems where queries and documents are not just plain text.[1]

Octen/OctenEmbedding8B is a text embedding model finetuned from Qwen/Qwen3Embedding8B, with 4096dimensional embeddings, 32,768token support in its listed model table, and a claimed 40,960token max sequence length elsewhere on the same page. Its model card claims 1 overall on the RTEB leaderboard with a Mean(Task) score of 0.8045, which is the strongest directly comparable textretrieval claim among the models in your list that I could verify.[3]

naverai/MuCo7B is a multimodal embedding model in the NAVER MuCo line, listed as based on Qwen/Qwen2VL7B and published as a featureextraction model. The associated collection describes MuCo as “Multiturn Contrastive Learning for Multimodal Embedding Model,” so this one appears oriented toward multimodal conversational or multiturn representation learning rather than plain textonly retrieval.[9][10]

caraai/ALM2Vec was only visible through a Hugging Face model index result showing ALM2VecPT and ALM2VecFT as 8B featureextraction models. Because I could not retrieve a verified model card or benchmark page for the exact root name caraai/ALM2Vec from the sources surfaced here, I would treat it as insufficiently documented for confident production selection based on this evidence alone.[11]

 Practical differences

For pure text retrieval, the strongest verified choices in this set are Octen/OctenEmbedding8B, Nemotron3Embed8BBF16, QZhouEmbedding, and BGEM3, but they occupy different points on the costquality curve. Octen and Nemotron are positioned as highend 8B models with leaderboardoriented claims, QZhou looks especially strong for Chinesecentric text workloads, and BGEM3 is much smaller and easier to run while still covering 100+ languages and multiple retrieval modes.[2][6][3][4]

For multimodal retrieval, Qwen/Qwen3VLEmbedding8B is the most clearly documented option here, because its model page explicitly supports text, images, screenshots, videos, and mixed inputs. MuCo7B is also multimodal, but the surfaced sources provide less operational detail than Qwen’s card, so Qwen is easier to recommend with confidence from the evidence available.[10][9][1]

 Best fit by use case

| Use case | Best pick | Why |
||||
| Lightweight multilingual text RAG | BAAI/bgem3 | Small 568M model, 100+ languages, dense/sparse/multivector support, longdocument handling up to 8192 tokens. [2] |
| Highestend text retrieval | Octen/OctenEmbedding8B | Finetuned from Qwen3Embedding8B and claims 1 RTEB overall with 4096dim embeddings. [3] |
| Multilingual enterprisestyle text search | nvidia/Nemotron3Embed8BBF16 | Positioned for RAG and crosslingual retrieval, with a claim of 1 on multilingual RTEB. [6] |
| Chinesefocused text embedding | KingsoftLLM/QZhouEmbedding | 7B text embedding model with strong MTEB/CMTEB claims and 8k context. [4] |
| Multimodal search | Qwen/Qwen3VLEmbedding8B | Explicit support for text, image, video, screenshots, and mixed inputs. [1] |
| Experimental multimodal alternative | naverai/MuCo7B | Multimodal embedding direction, but less fully documented in the retrieved sources. [9][10] |
| Underdocumented choice | caraai/ALM2Vec | Present in model index, but not enough verified detail surfaced for a strong recommendation. [11] |

 Recommended ranking

If I were choosing today for textonly production retrieval, I would rank them approximately as Octen/OctenEmbedding8B first, nvidia/Nemotron3Embed8BBF16 second, KingsoftLLM/QZhouEmbeddingZh or its closely related QZhouEmbedding variant third for Chineseheavy usage, and BAAI/bgem3 as the best efficiency baseline rather than the absolute best quality model. That ranking reflects the benchmark claims and model sizes visible in the retrieved sources, not a unified headtohead benchmark run across all eight names.[6][2][3][4]

For multimodal retrieval, I would put Qwen/Qwen3VLEmbedding8B first because its capabilities are the most explicitly documented and broadest in modality coverage among the retrieved results, with MuCo7B as a secondary option if your stack specifically benefits from NAVER’s multimodal contrastive setup. The Jina and ALM2Vec entries remain harder to rank responsibly here because the exact model pages were not verified in the surfaced sources.[9][10][11][1]

 Selection advice

Choose BGEM3 if you want a proven open multilingual baseline that is easier to deploy and cheap enough to use widely. Choose Octen or Nemotron when retrieval quality matters more than model size, choose QZhou when Chinese performance is central, and choose Qwen3VLEmbedding8B when your documents or queries include images or video rather than just text.[2][3][4][1][6]
